title_original: The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office
excerpt_original: Sony and Marvel’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day crossed the $1 billion mark at the global box office in five days this year, becoming the second-fastest film in history to hit the milestone, behind 2019’s Avengers: Endgame. Christopher Nolan’s epic, The Odyssey, also sailed into the…

blocks.text: Sony and Marvel’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day crossed the $1 billion mark at the global box office in five days this year, becoming the second-fastest film in history to hit the milestone, behind 2019’s Avengers: Endgame. Christopher Nolan’s epic, The Odyssey , also sailed into the billion-dollar threshold, making this a great year for Universal releases.
RELATED: 20 Great Films That Flopped At The Box Office From ‘Digger’ To ‘Fight Club’ And ‘Citizen Kane’

links.text: 20 Great Films That Flopped At The Box Office From ‘Digger’ To ‘Fight Club’ And ‘Citizen Kane’

blocks.text: They join Disney/Pixar’s Toy Story 5 and Lionsgate and Universal’s Michael , which passed the $1 billion mark to set a record as the most successful biopic in history and mark a historic first for Lionsgate, as well as Universal, Illumination, and Nintendo’s animated sequel The Super Mario Galaxy Movie , which reached the milestone in early June. Together, these releases continue to expand the exclusive club of films to reach the $1 billion club, alongside 2023’s The Super Mario Bros. Movie and 2021’s Spider-Man: No Way Home .
RELATED: The Top-Grossing Movies At The Box Office Every Year Since 1977

links.text: The Top-Grossing Movies At The Box Office Every Year Since 1977

blocks.text: Among the elite list of billion-dollar-grossing films are sequels, Disney remakes and iconic franchises such as Star Wars, Avatar, James Bond, The Lord of the Rings, the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Harry Potter, The Fast & The Furious, Jurassic Park , The Dark Knight, Transformers and Disney and Pixar toons.

The 2023 summer smash Barbie , starring Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling, propelled Greta Gerwig into the rankings as the first solo female director to reach the 10-digit milestone. Jennifer Lee hit the billion level with Disney’s Frozen II (2019), co-directing alongside Chris Buck.
